A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STL research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–I support reliable comparison. V3 additionally includes a NeurIPS reporting checklist.

before.justification: V2 reports original STL experiments on WebShop, HotpotQA and Game-of-24, including ablations, scaling results and efficiency analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and reports additional baseline, validation and self-improvement analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the fixed policy, lookahead targets, action-outcome rationales, value-model fine-tuning and simulated-lookahead inference. Depth-specific value models already appear in v2 Appendix D.3. The added greedy-search pseudocode and implementation disclosures do not establish a changed STL method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate WebShop shopping, HotpotQA retrieval-based question answering and Game-of-24 puzzles. Added validation splits and training-task counts remain within this coverage. Newly cited benchmarks such as BrowseComp and BabyAI are not evaluated.

E2.justification: V3 adds no-search ReACT and a qwen3-8b greedy value-model baseline on WebShop (Table 4). It also repairs Reflexion's conversational prompts and memory implementation (Appendix D.6). These are targeted additions and revisions; comparator sets for HotpotQA and Game-of-24 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 changes the value-only ablation to output-only loss, adds a 50-tasks-per-iteration Game-of-24 experiment and a 50-example held-out discount-factor validation. Figure 5 changes from costs including fine-tuning to inference-only costs and excludes reward-guided methods from the Pareto frontier. The reported WebShop training count changes from approximately 1500 to 1161, although Appendix D.2 says 1162; this does not establish that the main experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The rationale ablation is substantively revised through improved loss masking. New analyses test whether more tasks per iteration prevent early Game-of-24 deterioration (Appendix F.5), validate the discount factor on held-out data, and recheck mini-set performance after discovering an extra discounting instruction. V2's existing discount sweep and second-iteration WebShop failure analysis are retained.

E5.justification: V3 Table 5 adds error bars to existing full-test WebShop results. Their type and calculation are not defined, and no repeated-run count is supplied. The paired-bootstrap significance tests and one million bootstrap samples in Appendix I remain unchanged.

E6.justification: After Reflexion implementation repairs, Table 1 replaces its WebShop mini-set score/SR of 58.5/24.0 with 77.2/46.0, and full-set 49.5/16.4 with 72.9/41.3. After changing loss masking, Table 2 replaces the value-only score of 70.9 with 76.0; STL remains 78.3. V3 also adds baseline results, 48.0% Game-of-24 accuracy with 50 tasks per iteration, and validation rewards of 73.5 versus 72.7 for discount factors 1.0 versus 0.95. These are revised-setting or newly reported results; principal STL scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–6 are retained, with no new theorem, proof or derivation. Algorithm 2 restates the existing greedy search procedure. The expanded value-iteration analogy and applicability discussion do not introduce formal theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central claims remain reward-free value-model self-improvement, performance comparable to larger proprietary value models, and cheaper search. The rewritten abstract foregrounds the previously reported 39% WebShop improvement and QA/puzzle coverage; the introduction and conclusion retain their substantive contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 6 and expanded limitations identify action diversity, reliable later-state estimates, consistent transitions and language grounding as conditions for STL. Game-of-24's initial deterioration is reinterpreted as insufficient training-task exposure. WebShop discussion changes from outperforming reward-guided methods to performing similarly, while Appendix D.3 acknowledges the narrower advantage over value-only training and uncertainty about its cause.

D1.justification: V3 newly documents the attribute-specific value prompt and score adjustment, loss masking, training-example details, 30 MCTS evaluation iterations, temperature 1.0 and max_tokens 3192. It describes Reflexion repairs, the discovered discounting instruction and incomplete reruns, and distinguishes data-generation costs, fine-tuning costs and inference pricing, including Azure model-version details. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the code link and principal hardware/hyperparameter disclosures were already present.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations and discussion concerning grounded environments, agent-specific tuning and reinforcement-learning agents, including BabyAI, BrowseComp, Group-in-group Policy Optimization and WebAgent-R1. ExpeL is added in the Reflexion discussion. The broader positioning around reward-free self-improvement and fitted value iteration remains intact.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the abstract, inserts an applicability discussion, expands several appendix explanations, reorders Appendices A–C, reorganizes cost subsections and appends a reporting checklist. Most existing background, method and experimental prose is retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: V3 adds three compact appendix tables, an attribute-prompt panel, a training-rationale example and greedy-search pseudocode. Figure 5 is relocated and redrawn with revised score axes, gold reward-guided markers and a restricted Pareto frontier. Existing principal diagrams and table structures largely remain, alongside local spacing, pagination and algorithm-formatting changes.

improvement.justification: V3 repairs two important weaknesses in v2's empirical evidence: malfunctioning Reflexion comparisons and a disadvantaged value-only ablation (Appendices D.6 and D.3). These corrections, the added generalization analysis and concrete applicability limits make the paper substantially more credible, even though STL's comparative advantages become narrower. Cost accounting is more explicit, although the plotted comparison now excludes one-time costs. Undefined error bars and incomplete rechecking after the discounting issue remain limitations.
